title: Rav Yehuda bar Yishmael
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Chullin 118b in a halakhic discussion. It appears to Hyman that he is the one who is always called in the Yerushalmi by the name Rabbi Yudan bei Rabbi Yishmael.

He was a great man and maintained a great academy, as in Yerushalmi Berakhot ch. 4, halakha 2: Rabbi Yudan bei Rabbi Yishmael instructed his public interpreter to recite after his exposition (the prayer of Rabbi Chiyya bar Vava) thus. And there, ch. 5, halakha 1, that he would meditate on words of Torah so intensely that his cloak fell off, and a snake guarded it so that no one else would take it; his students said to him, "Rabbi, here is your cloak lying on the ground." He said to them, "And is that wicked creature not careful about it?" And in Nedarim ch. 4, halakha 3, he permitted teachers of children to take payment, and said that they take payment for lost time (from work). So it is also cited in the Ran, Nedarim 36. And in Shabbat ch. 1, halakha 4, he said that the court disagreed with him (Rabbi Yehuda Nesia) concerning divorce. And there, ch. 3, halakha 2, Rabbi Yudan bei Rabbi Yishmael ruled, because of pressure, to rake out an oven, etc. And there, ch. 6, halakha 2, it is related that his foot was worn away from a wound and he put on a hobnailed sandal. And the view of Mavo HaYerushalmi is that he was the brother of Ulla (without further qualification) bar Yishmael.

notes.text: Amora in the academy passage means the public interpreter, not a new named amora. The court is said to disagree with Rabbi Yehuda Nesia. Hyman’s proposed identity with the Yerushalmi Yudan and the proposed brotherhood with Ulla remain attributed.

Chullin 118b directly names Yehudah bar Yishmael in the pomegranate discussion. It does not establish Hyman’s tentative identity with the Jerusalem Talmud Yudan or the reported brotherhood with Ulla. His always wording remains attributed, and the public interpreter is a role rather than a newly named amora.
